lesson_title: The Bag of Sweets That Breaks Everyone's First Answer
hook_text: Three colours in the bag. So blue is one in three... right? Wrong — and here's the count that proves it.
clip_script: Ten sweets in a packet: 5 red, 3 blue, 2 green. Shake well, close your eyes, take one. What is the chance it is blue? The tempting answer says one colour in three — a third. But watch what actually happens at your fingertips: your hand meets TEN sweets, and every single sweet has an equal chance of being grabbed. Red is not one candidate — red is five candidates wearing the same shirt. So the real question is: ten possible grabs, how many are blue? Three. The probability is 3 out of 10 — 0,3, not 0,33. Count things, never types. And the same two counts answer everything: red or green? Five plus two happy grabs out of ten — 0,7. Not green? One minus 2 tenths — 0,8. Two counts and a divide. That is the whole engine of probability.
visual_style: Macro shot of a sweet packet spilling into a circle, each sweet lighting up as a counter with its own ticket, the wrong '1/3' stamp shattering as ten tickets fan out, then quick-fire fraction overlays for each question.
pacing: Hook and trap answer fast, slow-motion beat on the ten tickets reveal, rapid triple-hit of the three computed answers.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master both engines of probability.
